title: Least privilege and IAM best practices

kcs.statement: The principle of least privilege means granting an identity only the permissions it needs for its task, starting from none and adding more only when required.
IAM best practice is to assign permissions through groups, use roles for applications and cross-account access, require MFA, rotate long-term credentials, and never share credentials.

The IAM credential report lists every user and the status of their passwords, access keys and MFA, and IAM access advisor shows which services an identity last used, so unused permissions can be removed.
